Briefing for 11 November 2026

Short items for 11 November 2026. Sapaude writes them in its own words. Where a longer article exists, the link goes there. The publisher is Sapaude.

New model

Gemini 4 Carbon is out for developers and Ultra users

Google released Gemini 4 Carbon, its strongest model for long agentic tasks and cybersecurity. Via API it costs $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens, the same introductory price as Gemini 4 Argon.

Source: Google

Everyday tool

Anthropic sets IPO range at $70 to $78 per share

Anthropic started its IPO roadshow and plans to offer 825 million shares on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT. The registration is not yet effective; CNBC's sources expect pricing on November 18.

Source: Anthropic

Everyday tool

Companies can now claim their profile in ChatGPT

OpenAI launched Businesses in ChatGPT in beta: firms can update their details and see aggregated mention and click data. Eligible US online shops can also publish Business Agents that answer customer questions.

Source: OpenAI

New model

Gemini Robotics 2.5 sorts car parts in a Mercedes pilot

Google DeepMind's new vision-language-action model helped Apptronik humanoids sort parts on Mercedes-Benz lines in Hungary and Germany. DeepMind reports a 96% success rate in this proof of concept.

Source: Google DeepMind

AI agents · More technical

AI agents formally verify Signal's encryption code

Google DeepMind's AlphaProof Code used prover agents and human-reviewed Lean specifications to check security properties of Signal's compiled code. The proofs are public on GitHub.

Source: Google DeepMind

New model

MiniMax opens H3-Image for fast 4K image generation

MiniMax released open weights for H3-Image, which generates and edits images up to 4096 by 4096 pixels and can use up to 16 reference images. MiniMax says a 4K image takes under 10 seconds.

Source: MiniMax

Everyday tool

Alexa+ now works in the browser in Germany

Amazon opened Alexa.com to Alexa+ early-access users in Germany; the assistant now handles shopping, smart-home control and planning on laptops and desktops, not just on Echo devices and in the app.

Source: Amazon

Be brave. Get smart.
